# Antenna communication benchmark

Reproducible **SISO, fixed-power** antenna BER/EVM experiments using GNU Radio, Python, MATLAB, and eventually USRP radios. There is one transmit RF stream and one receive RF stream. The primary waveform is legacy 20 MHz non-HT OFDM, with BPSK, QPSK, 16-QAM, and 64-QAM. Electronic steering and mechanical orientation are recorded separately.

**Current results are software simulations. No antenna gain, RF link performance, live steering, or standards certification has been measured.** The Wi-Fi waveform replay uses actual PPDUs generated by MATLAB WLAN Toolbox. Its independent metric receivers currently receive packet timing, rate, and length from the experiment metadata.

Start here: [Editing the benchmark as an RF engineer](docs/MODULAR_FLOWGRAPHS.md) — which knob to change, reusable module diagrams, and how to preserve your edits.

## Start with the live SISO labs

```sh
cd /Users/ofi/repos/grc
antenna-grc grc/siso_modem_lab.grc grc/siso_wlan_lab.grc
```

Generate (F5), Execute (F6), Stop (F7). Both graphs contain the transmit/channel/receive chain and calculate BER/EVM while running. The windows include equalized/reference constellation, TX/RX spectrum, waterfall, I/Q time views, and numerical BER/EVM. Parameters stay fixed per run. Exact integer counts and configuration are saved when stopping. Read the [SISO lab guide](docs/SISO_LABS.md) for every parameter, signal stage, display and output file.

The initial antenna experiment stays simple: **set beam → settle → capture a fixed block → calculate pre-FEC BER, EVM and received power**. Known-rate PHY bursts provide training; no Wi-Fi association, MAC acknowledgements or retransmissions are implemented. Post-FEC/PER curves remain optional validation material.

## Reproduce all software results

Use the radioconda Python interpreter with GNU Radio, NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, and PyYAML. MATLAB requires Communications Toolbox and WLAN Toolbox. No radio is needed, and this command never launches the hardware graphs.

```sh
cd /Users/ofi/repos/grc
/Users/ofi/radioconda/bin/python scripts/run_all.py
```

For another machine, run `python scripts/run_all.py --matlab /path/to/matlab` from the repository. `MATLAB_BIN` may also specify the MATLAB executable. All project file paths are computed relative to the source tree; generated MATLAB and GNU Radio artifacts require the corresponding installed tools.

The runner generates exact theory and independent Monte Carlo results, exports all eight legacy Wi-Fi rates, compiles four reusable modules and seven top-level GRC graphs, and executes only the five software graphs. It independently analyzes every Wi-Fi rate in Python and MATLAB, checks native CP removal/FFT, runs 34 complete finite Qt SISO cases with actual plotting sinks/event loops, runs tests, and writes logs and a source-hash manifest. The two UHD hardware graphs are compiled only. Outputs are replaced on rerun; copy an experiment's `results/` directory elsewhere before generating a different study.

On this Mac the local package is installed in `.venv` with access to radioconda libraries. Double-click [Open Benchmark GRC.command](<Open Benchmark GRC.command>) to open all seven flowgraphs, or run `antenna-grc`. The launcher supplies the correct interpreter and PATH. For a fresh installation, first run `python -m pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .` using the GNU Radio Python environment. See [flowgraph setup](docs/FLOWGRAPHS.md).

The runner checks all four modulation orders, strict finite capture lengths for all eight Wi-Fi rates, every rate's native GRC FFT, fixed-power SISO sweeps, and multipath/CFO receiver controls. It regenerates [the primary Markdown report](results/REPORT.md) with five SISO figures and an [appendix](results/VALIDATION_APPENDIX.md) with the eight earlier theory/reference figures and complete simulation tables.

Charts also have vector PDF exports; the Python overview/comparison figures have SVG exports. CSV files accompany the results. Do not digitize the chart images when the underlying data are available.

## Main entry points

- `matlab/run_theory.m`: exact BER calculation, Communications Toolbox oracle, Monte Carlo, and four charts.
- `matlab/run_wlan_awgn.m`: separate coded WLAN receiver simulation and BER/PER charts.
- `matlab/export_wlan_reference.m`: reproducible true non-HT reference PPDUs and metadata.
- `matlab/analyze_wlan_capture.m`: independent post-FEC decoder and EVM cross-check for aligned captures.
- `scripts/run_python_reference.py`: independent uncoded Monte Carlo and shared fixtures.
- `scripts/analyze_symbols.py`: score the symbol-rate GRC capture.
- `scripts/analyze_wlan.py`: independent FFT/L-LTF equalization, EVM, and mapped coded-bit BER.
- `antenna_steering.py`: mock command execution and a replaceable hardware backend contract.

The user's original `test_flow.py` and `test_flow.grc` are preserved and are not part of the benchmark runner.

The next hardware work is to identify the antenna band and daughterboards, validate a cabled RF baseline, integrate the actual steering protocol, implement autonomous/timed acquisition, and archive UHD stream health and actual settings. See the [methods](docs/PAPER_METHODS.md) before collecting paper measurements.
